p: Want to tip the scorecard in your favour? There's a bit of a knack to crazy golf. Take a second to read each hole before you hit, spotting the slope and the angle you'll need off the walls. Most of the time a gentle putt beats a big whack, because balls that go flying tend to bounce straight back to where they started. Holding the putter low and keeping your body still helps too.

House rules are worth agreeing before you start. Plenty of groups go with a six-shot maximum per hole, which keeps the round moving and stops any one player getting stuck behind a tricky obstacle. Little ones might get a free "do-over" or two to keep spirits up.

Braehead is a handy base for a bit more fun. The Xscape complex next door has the indoor Snow Factor slope among its leisure options, so the more adventurous can try skiing or snowboarding without leaving the area. And across the Clyde, the Riverside Museum, Glasgow's transport museum, is a brilliant free day out, with vintage trams, cars and a recreated old street to wander. The Tall Ship sits alongside it on the river.

Glasgow has plenty more for a full day, from the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum to a stroll along the river. Pair a round here with any of those and you've got a fun-packed day out whatever the weather.
